body.statement:
Define the restricted class
\[
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)
=\left\{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda):
P\text{ satisfies \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} and
\texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering}}\right\}.
\]
There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on fixed class constants, such that along every array with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), uniformly for \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\) and \(P\)-almost every \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\),
\[
cR_\star
\le\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le CR_\star.
\]
The raw feasible estimator in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator} attains the upper bound with nonidentically distributed bounded event outcomes, an unknown heteroskedastic donor law, and estimated full \(\Sigma\).
body.justification: The theorem gives the exact allocation frontier on the explicit subclass where calendar-shared conditional means cannot defeat replication.
body.gap: The original class fails by the retained shared-design obstruction, so stating the subclass is mathematically load-bearing rather than cosmetic.
body.consumer: Designers can compare donor, calendar-spacing, and cohort-replication investments without importing a hidden strict-exogeneity premise.
body.proof_tex:
By \texttt{lem:identification-fwl},
\[
\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_s\pi_s
\{\mathbb E[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\]
The equality conditions on \(z_0,E_0\), but \(z_0=\mathbb E[Z_j\mid E_0]\) is \(E_0\)-measurable.  Let \(\mathscr F\) be the complete historical design, event state, and donor sample.  Exactly as in \texttt{lem:exact-full-data-interval-calibration}, decompose
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=\mathcal E_{\mathrm{evt}}-\mathcal E_{\mathrm{hist}}
-\mathcal B_L-\mathcal B_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Full-design mean stability, historical full-design centering, donor independence, and conditional cross-unit independence give
\[
\mathbb E[\mathcal E_{\mathrm{evt}}\mid\mathscr F]
=\mathbb E[\mathcal E_{\mathrm{hist}}\mid\mathscr F]=0,
\]
\[
\mathbb E[\mathcal E_{\mathrm{evt}}^2\mid\mathscr F]
\le C\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}=CR_{\mathrm{tr}},
\]
and, by the weight bound in \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control},
\[
\mathbb E[\mathcal E_{\mathrm{hist}}^2\mid\mathscr F]
\le B^2\sum_{s,i}
\left[\pi_s\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le CR_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\]
The same lemma gives
\[
\mathbb E[\mathcal B_L^2\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]
\le C(R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}),
\qquad
\mathbb E[\mathcal B_{\mathrm{don}}^2\mid E_0]\le CR_{\mathrm{don}},
\]
and \(P(\mathrm{bad}\mid E_0)\le CR_\star\).  On failure the convention in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}, bounded outcomes, and the selected-weight bound keep squared loss bounded by a fixed class constant.  Applying
\((x_1+\cdots+x_4)^2\le4\sum_jx_j^2\) therefore yields
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M^\dagger}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le C(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee
R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}})
=CR_\star.
\]

For the converse fix a channel \(q\) and use the pair from
\texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}.  Write its target values as
\(\theta_0,\theta_1\) and \(\Delta_q=|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).
Given an arbitrary estimator, test the two laws by selecting the target
closest to the estimator.  On a testing error its squared estimation
error is at least \(\Delta_q^2/4\).  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_0[(\widetilde\tau-\theta_0)^2]
+\mathbb E_1[(\widetilde\tau-\theta_1)^2]
&\ge\frac{\Delta_q^2}{4}
\{P_0(\phi=1)+P_1(\phi=0)\}\\
&\ge\frac{\Delta_q^2}{4}
\int\min\{dP_{0,q},dP_{1,q}\}
\ge cR_q.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the maximum of the two risks is at least \(cR_q\).  Taking the
largest of the four channels gives \(cR_\star\).  All pairs lie in
\(\mathcal M^\dagger\), so the lower and upper bounds concern the same
full-design-centered causal panel class.  The covariance estimate may be
spectrally clipped because the estimator's centers use donor means and
the clipping eigenvalues stay within fixed multiples of the true
ellipticity bounds; no oracle covariance enters the fitted regression.
